title: Subprograms: procedures and functions
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Assembly line
objectives: know how to define a subprogram with def and how to call it
understand how a parameter passes a value into a subprogram and how return passes one back out
know the difference between a local variable and a global one
starter: A program defines a subprogram called banner with one print line inside it, and then stops. Nothing is printed when it runs. Explain why, and write down the line that has been left out.

stations.name: Writing a procedure
stations.fact: Writing a job once and calling it many times has a name of its own: code reuse.
stations.challenge: What is the difference between defining a procedure and calling it?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for a title. Write a procedure called signoff that prints end of report, then display [title] and call signoff, so the title comes first.

Ask the user for two headings, one on each line. Write a procedure called rule that prints =====, then display the rule, the first heading, the rule, the second heading and the rule, one on each line.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Parameters
stations.fact: The names in the definition are the parameters; the values handed over when it is called are the arguments.
stations.challenge: Why is a procedure with a parameter more useful than one without?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: Ask the user for two item names, one on each line. Write a procedure called label that takes one word and prints item: [word]. Call it once for each name, in the order they were typed.
Ask the user for the number of packs and then the price of one pack in pence. Write a procedure called charge that takes both and prints total [packs times price]. Call it, and print nothing else.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Returning a value
stations.fact: return ends the subprogram there and then, so any line written after it never runs.
stations.challenge: Why would a task insist a subprogram returns a value rather than prints it?

rows: Ask the user for a whole number. Write a function called double that returns twice its parameter and prints nothing at all, then display [what double hands back] and nothing else.

Ask the user for a width and then a height, both whole numbers. Write a function called area that returns width times height and holds no print at all. Store what it returns and display one line, area [that value].

stations.name: Functions and procedures
stations.fact: The exam marks this difference, so say 'function' only when a value actually comes back.
stations.challenge: Decide whether each subprogram in your program is a function or a procedure.

rows: Ask the user for a name and then a whole number mark. Write a function called grade that returns pass for a mark of 40 or more and fail below 40, and a procedure called report that displays [name]: [that word].

stations.name: Local and global
stations.fact: Keeping variables local is good practice: it stops one part of a program quietly breaking another.
stations.challenge: Why can two subprograms both use a variable called total without clashing?

rows: Ask the user for a whole number and keep it in a variable called total. Write a procedure called boost with a local total of its own, set to 99, that prints it. Call boost, then display [the main total].

Write a procedure called win that adds 3 to a shared score and a procedure called draw that adds 1. Ask the user for the number of rounds, call win and then draw once per round, and display [the final score].

stations.name: Putting it together
stations.fact: Breaking a problem into named parts is decomposition, which you met in topic 2.1.
stations.challenge: Plan which parts of a booking receipt program should become subprograms.

keyq: When should a subprogram return a value rather than print one?
exam: A subprogram called vat takes an amount and its last line is print(amount * 0.2). The main program writes tax = vat(50) and then prints tax, which shows None. Explain why, and write the change needed inside the subprogram.
Write a function that takes a length and a width in metres and returns the area, and a main program that uses it to print the area of two different rooms.
Write a procedure that takes a pupil's name and a score and prints one tidy line of a results table, then call it for three different pupils.
